title: Bob and Ray
paragraphs: Bob Elliott and Ray Goulding's long-running satirical comedy, built from deadpan sketches that spoofed broadcasting, advertising, interviews, soap operas, and everyday American life.

Bob Elliott and Ray Goulding’s long-running deadpan comedy/satire partnership. The historical broadcasts combined ad-libbed talk, sketches, mock interviews, serial parodies, characters, music and fake/real commercials across local, network and public radio. GRH’s current 1,837 playable objects are predominantly track-level compilation segments rather than one-to-one broadcast episodes, so broadcast metadata is never inferred merely from track order.

GRH documents the program through WHDH Boston era (1946 to July 1, 1951) on [[org|org.957c02c01469be51|WHDH]], NBC network era (July 2, 1951 to October 9, 1953) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], NBC Monitor participation (1955 to 1959) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and Mutual daily era (October 3, 1955 to September 20, 1957) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].
Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include Soap opera parody, Mock interviews, Advertising parody, Journalism, Book reviewing, and Sports broadcasting.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Postwar radio culture as material for satire, Bob and Ray across the network-radio/television transition, and Advertising culture and Bob and Ray’s mock commercials.
